newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices narrowly mixed, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices narrowly mixed, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were narrowly mixed Tuesday in lackluster trade, with relatively firm crude and the approach of winter tempered by the lack of East Coast utility demand, industry sources said.
"Utility demand is not here yet, but there's an upward bias ahead of winter. If you have inventory, why sell it before the heating season?" said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs were steady to up slightly, with 2.2 percent now talked at $20.75 a barrel and three percent unchanged at $19.75-20.00, traders said.

Prompt one percent in New York was little changed at $21.25-50, with November paper reportedly done at $21.50 and $21.55, also steady on the day. December paper remained talked on either side of $21.60, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was steady to down slightly at about $20, while three percent notionally eased to the $19.75 area on prospects for better supplies soon.

New York City gate gas prices firmed about 10 cents Tuesday to the low-$2.90s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.39/mmBtu equivalent. November New York gas was quoted at NYMEX plus 65 cents, or in the $3.25-3.30/mmBtu area, while December was pegged at NYMEX plus $1.10, or about $3.80/mmBtu.
